evidence: createApp registers Express routes such as app.post("/projects/:projectId/tasks"), and each one calls a service like services.tasks.create or services.tasks.markDone. This is transport work.
bodyOf, requiredString, optionalString, optionalDate, queryString and param only check the type and format of the HTTP input.
parseStatus checks values with the domain's isTaskStatus and TASK_STATUSES, so it does not re-implement the domain rule.
The error middleware maps ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError to 400, 404 and 409. Mapping errors to HTTP codes is an infrastructure job.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts is an Express HTTP adapter, and everything it does belongs to infrastructure (transport). It sets up routes and middleware, checks the shape of request bodies, query strings and path parameters, parses ISO dates, turns domain errors into HTTP status codes, and serialises responses. Each route passes the work to an application service (users, projects, tasks) and makes no business decisions itself. The status parser checks values with the domain's isTaskStatus and TASK_STATUSES rather than keeping its own copy of the rule. Defaulting a missing description to "" is input normalisation, not a business invariant. Nothing here does persistence or carries a domain rule that belongs in another layer.
